content: Lamivudine and nevirapine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome, so caution and monitoring are advised. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of lapatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. It increases the levels or effects of lemborexant through the same mechanism, necessitating close monitoring and potential dose adjustments, especially with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Letermovir increases nevirapine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Nevirapine reduces the levels of levonorgestrel (both intrauterine and oral forms) and lidocaine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, warranting caution and monitoring. Similarly, it decreases the levels of linagliptin, potentially through other mechanisms, and hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. Nevirapine increases lomitapide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and the lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. It decreases lopinavir, loratadine, losartan, maraviroc, medroxyprogesterone, mefloquine, meloxicam, meperidine, mestranol, methadone, methylprednisolone, and midazolam levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Intranasal midazolam levels may increase, potentially prolonging sedation when co-administered with mild CYP3A4 inhibitors. Nevirapine decreases mifepristone and mirtazapine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Mitotane reduces nevirapine levels as it is a strong CYP3A4 inducer, requiring dose adjustments and monitoring. Nevirapine decreases modafinil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and nafcillin reduces nevirapine levels through the same pathway. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. Nevirapine reduces nefazodone levels, potentially decreasing toxicity. It decreases nelfinavir levels, but both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Nelfinavir increases nevirapine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Nevirapine reduces nicardipine, nifedipine, nilotinib, nisoldipine, and osilodrostat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating close monitoring and therapy adjustments. Orlistat reduces nevirapine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, potentially leading to loss of virological control in HIV-infected patients. Frequent monitoring of HIV RNA levels is recommended, and orlistat should be discontinued if viral load increases. Nevirapine decreases ospemifene levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and oxcarbazepine reduces nevirapine levels through the same pathway. Nevirapine decreases oxycodone, pazopanib, phenobarbital, phenytoin, pimavanserin, and posaconazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Posaconazole increases nevirapine levels, potentially increasing toxicity. Nevirapine reduces praziquantel, prednisone, primidone, quetiapine, quinidine, and repaglinide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Ribociclib increases nevirapine levels, while rifabutin and rifapentine reduce nevirapine levels by increasing metabolism. Nevirapine decreases riociguat, risperidone, and ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, but ritonavir increases nevirapine levels. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Rucaparib increases nevirapine levels, requiring therapy adjustments and monitoring. Nevirapine decreases selegiline, sertraline, sildenafil, solifenacin, sorafenib, sunitinib, suvorexant, tacrolimus, tadalafil, tamoxifen, tasimelteon, tazemetostat, and tecovirimat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce the efficacy of these drugs. Nevirapine decreases temsirolimus, teniposide, theophylline, ticagrelor, tinidazole, tipranavir, tofacitinib, tolterodine, toremifene, tramadol, triamcinolone, triazolam, and ubrogepant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring close monitoring and therapy adjustments. Tipranavir and nevirapine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Nevirapine decreases valoctocogene roxaparvovec, vardenafil, verapamil, vilazodone, voriconazole, vortioxetine, zidovudine, and other drug levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Zidovudine and nevirapine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Nevirapine interacts with various other drugs, including acetazolamide, alosetron, ambrisentan, amitriptyline, anastrozole, atazanavir, black cohosh, bosentan, caspofungin, cevimeline, clarithromycin, clomipramine, cyclophosphamide, danazol, dapsone, disopyramide, docetaxel, donepezil, drospirenone, dutasteride, eplerenone, eucalyptus, imatinib, imipramine, isradipine, itraconazole, ketoconazole, lansoprazole, larotrectinib, levoketoconazole, montelukast, nimodipine, nitrendipine, ondansetron, oxybutynin, paclitaxel, parecoxib, pimozide, pioglitazone, propafenone, quinine, rabeprazole, ramelteon, rifampin, ruxolitinib, saxagliptin, sufentanil, vinblastine, vincristine, vinorelbine, zaleplon, and others, primarily by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Most interactions require caution, monitoring, and potential dose adjustments.
